do_more: Start with a concrete, everyday scenario that viewers instantly recognize
Use a single, punchy hook word (Trap, Curve, Dilemma, Paradox) to frame the psychology concept
Keep the script to the standard length (~42 seconds) to allow a clear setup, conflict, and payoff
Inject a surprise or twist midway to boost re‑watchability
End with a memorable, actionable takeaway that ties back to the opening hook
avoid: Generic titles without a hook (e.g., “How to…”)
Repeating the same hook word across multiple episodes
Over‑loading the short with too many facts – stay on one core idea
Using emojis or overly cute phrasing that dilutes the curiosity factor
short.title_style: Use the pattern ‘The [Unexpected Situation] [Hook Word]’ – a concise, curiosity‑driving phrase that signals a relatable dilemma and a psychological twist
next_tests: Film a 45‑second ‘standard’ episode that opens with a question title like ‘Why Does Your Brain Freeze at 3 AM?’ and compare VPD
Swap the hook word ‘Trap’ for alternatives such as ‘Paradox’, ‘Dilemma’, or ‘Loop’ across three videos to see which drives higher avg‑watch %
Add a visual metaphor (e.g., a bouncing ball) that appears only at the 20‑second mark and measure its impact on re‑watch rates
